title: Paul McCartney jams with Denny Laine and Denny Seiwell | 1971
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney invited guitarist Denny Laine and drummer Denny Seiwell to join them in Scotland in July 1971.

McCartney was planning to form a band, and had previously played with Seiwell on the Ram album. Its guitarist Hugh McCracken had declined McCartney’s band offer, but Seiwell was keen. McCartney turned instead to former Moody Blues member Laine, who was working as a songwriter for hire at the time.

Seiwell and his wife Monique left New York on 19 July, arriving at the McCartneys’ High Park Farm on 21 July. Laine also arrived that day, having travelled up from London.

The McCartneys and their guests jammed together for the first time on 22 July. Paul played them outtakes from the Ram sessions, plus new songs he had been working on, including ‘Tomorrow’, ‘I Am Your Singer’, ‘Bip Bop’, and ‘Wild Life’. They also jammed a reggae-style song initially known as ‘Half Past Ten’, but which became ‘Love Is Strange’.

Events moved quickly. A week of recording sessions was booked at EMI Studios from 24 July, so on the 23rd Linda arranged a private flight to take the musicians and their equipment to London.
